text: In sensor networks. Now, remember what we said before. In general, in device-to-device communication networks, we need distributed algorithms. Right, there is no central node that tells everyone what to do. The nodes make their own decisions. So that holds also for channel access. We need schemes. At each node, each single node needs to observe the channel, and decide when to access, based on what this node observes, independently of the others. Okay. So a very good, typically a very good, strategy would be to design a protocol, a Mark protocol. That in spite of the fact that we have this distributed approach, is able to avoid collisions. Right, so we want to avoid the case where multiple nodes start transmitting at the same time, and their transmissions may cause a collision at the receiver. That's something that we want to avoid. Okay. And it's in particular important to do so when we apply in the distributed channel access schemes. Okay, because in that case indeed, certain nodes, different nodes, since they make decisions independently, they may decide to access at the same time. So.
